propositions: The operator hypothesis that completion verification works well as a plain subagent harness with free tools and that unreliability stems from in-process scaffolding rather than the task itself must be tested directly by comparing production verifier against minimal harness agent on the same corpus.

Arm B (minimal harness agent using Copilot CLI) produced 5 false-FAILs on real ACs (all on 0e68 epic) while Arm A (production in-process verifier) produced 0 false-FAILs, failing the predeclared GO condition (ii).
Arm B median wall time (415.5s) exceeded 2× Arm A median wall time (262s threshold), failing predeclared GO condition (iii); Arm A achieved 100% per-AC agreement vs Arm B's 94.6%.
Both arms achieved 0 false-PASS verdicts on planted-unmet ACs, meeting predeclared GO condition (i) but insufficient alone.

The 0e68 epic AC7 and AC2 rejections by Arm B represent plausibly defensible strict-literal readings of coverage gaps (commitment mutations in separate commits, empty enrichment maps in test client) rather than tooling-induced failures.
